package_info.why_malicious: The package was compromised via a software supply chain attack, allowing the Agrius APT group to distribute the Fantasy wiper malware to downstream customers. The update mechanism was abused to deliver destructive code intended solely to wipe data, causing irrecoverable damage to victims in the diamond industry and related sectors.

execution_context.file_location: delivered via the Israeli suite developer's update mechanism

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Fantasy wiper malware (exact code not shown in report, but described as a destructive data wiper built off Apostle wiper)
malicious_snippets.code_language: Unknown (likely C/C++ or .NET, based on prior wiper malware)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon execution via a compromised software update, the code systematically overwrites or deletes files on the victim's system, rendering data unrecoverable and causing operational disruption.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code's sole purpose is to destroy data, not to provide any legitimate functionality or even extort ransom. It is delivered through a trusted software update channel, making it highly deceptive.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software updates are expected to deliver bug fixes or new features, not destructive payloads. The presence of a data wiper in an update is a severe violation of trust.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate disk wiping tools exist for secure data erasure, but are never distributed via automatic software updates to unsuspecting users.
key_indicators: Destructive file overwrite and deletion routines
Execution triggered by a software update
No ransom demand or recovery mechanism
Code lineage linked to known wiper malware (Apostle)

attack_chain.action: Agrius APT compromises the Israeli suite developer's software update mechanism.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious update is distributed to customers.

attack_chain.action: Victim organizations receive and install the malicious update.
attack_chain.leads_to: Fantasy wiper malware is executed on victim systems.

attack_chain.action: Fantasy wiper executes, systematically destroying data on infected systems.
attack_chain.leads_to: Operational disruption and data loss at targeted organizations.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected file overwrite or deletion activity immediately following a software update
Execution of unknown binaries delivered via update mechanisms
Absence of ransom note or recovery instructions after destructive activity
file_indicators: Presence of new or modified executables in update directories
Unusual file access patterns (mass deletion/overwrite) by update processes
network_indicators: Unusual connections to update servers outside normal update windows
Potential C2 or telemetry traffic if wiper attempts to report success (not confirmed for Fantasy)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for anomalous file system activity (mass deletion/overwrite) immediately after software updates, especially from processes associated with update mechanisms. Correlate with update logs to identify unexpected or unauthorized update payloads. Use endpoint detection to flag execution of binaries with destructive behavior, and investigate any new executables delivered via trusted update channels.
